runs.v: A commercial roofing system is a multi-layered assembly-membrane, insulation, deck, vapor barriers, flashings, drainage, and accessories-engineered to protect a building from water, wind, UV exposure, and thermal stress. Flat and low-slope commercial roofs, which dominate Newark's skyline, require fundamentally different solutions than residential pitched roofs because they must manage water drainage across near-level surfaces, support heavy rooftop equipment, and withstand decades of freeze–thaw cycling.

Newark-specific factors make system selection especially important. Many commercial buildings here sit on older brick and masonry structures with parapets that demand precise flashing and edge detailing. Mixed-use properties may have multiple roof levels. Heavy foot traffic from HVAC technicians is common, and snow loads in winter followed by intense summer heat and humidity create punishing thermal cycles. All of these drive both material choice and installation quality.
Key Components of a Commercial Roof Assembly

Every commercial roof assembly starts with the deck-steel, concrete, or wood-which provides the structural foundation. Above the deck sits a vapor barrier to control moisture migration, followed by insulation boards (typically polyisocyanurate or EPS) that deliver thermal performance and help meet New Jersey's

. Cover boards protect insulation from damage and improve fire ratings. The membrane-TPO, EPDM, PVC, modified bitumen, or BUR-is the primary waterproofing layer. Flashings seal every edge, penetration, and transition. Drainage devices (internal drains, scuppers, gutters) move water off the roof and prevent ponding.

Each component directly affects durability, energy performance, and code compliance. Insulation R-values, for example, have been rising through successive NJ energy code cycles, and polyisocyanurate remains the most popular above-deck insulation product. Many re-roof projects now require upgraded insulation even when the membrane itself is still serviceable. Tapered insulation-creating a minimum ½-inch per foot slope-is often critical for eliminating ponding water, which is one of the leading causes of premature membrane failure.

Low-Slope vs. Steep-Slope Commercial Roofs

Low-slope roofs-defined as having a pitch of 3:12 or less-are the standard on warehouses, shopping centers, industrial buildings, and most office structures across Newark. These roofs require membrane-based roofing systems that effectively shed water across relatively flat surfaces. Single ply membranes (TPO, EPDM, PVC), BUR, modified bitumen, SPF, and roof coating systems are the primary solutions for low-slope applications.

Steep-slope commercial roofs appear on churches, historic buildings, and smaller retail properties with visible rooflines. These typically pair with metal roofing, slate, architectural shingles, or tile, where aesthetic value and long-term performance matter as much as waterproofing. Some commercial properties combine both-flat sections for mechanical equipment and steep-slope sections facing the street.
Understanding your roof type and structure is the starting point for choosing the right commercial roofing solution.

TPO (Thermoplastic Polyolefin) Roofing Systems

TPO roofing is popular for low-slope applications and has become one of the most widely installed single ply roofing membranes on Newark shopping centers, warehouses, and office buildings since the early 2000s. Its white, highly reflective surface reduces cooling costs with heat-reflective properties, making it a proven choice where summer energy consumption is a concern. Seams are heat-welded, creating bonds that are stronger and more watertight than adhesive or tape methods. TPO roofing costs range from $5 to $8 per square foot for the membrane, though fully installed commercial systems in NJ-including insulation, tear-off, and flashing-typically run $7 to $14 per square foot in 2026.
A typical 10,000-square-foot

in Newark costs roughly $70,000 to $110,000 depending on penetration count and insulation requirements. Expected lifespan is 20 to 30 years when installation quality is high and drainage is properly designed. Newer TPO formulations have improved UV stability and seam strength, further extending long term performance.

runs.v: EPDM (Rubber) Roofing Systems

EPDM roofing is effective in handling temperature extremes, which makes it exceptionally well suited for New Jersey's freeze–thaw cycles. This black synthetic rubber single ply membrane has a proven track record stretching back to the 1970s on schools, industrial buildings, and distribution centers throughout Essex County. Its flexibility at low temperatures resists cracking and splitting that can plague other materials during harsh winters.

EPDM roofing typically costs between $4 and $7 per square foot for materials, with fully installed commercial systems in Newark running approximately $6.50 to $11 per square foot. Service life is typically 20 to 30 years, with premium 90-mil membranes approaching 35 years under ideal conditions. The primary trade-off is that

absorbs solar heat, increasing cooling loads in summer-though white EPDM variants are available. Seams are adhesive or tape-bonded, which are generally weaker than heat-welded seams found in TPO and PVC.

Excellent weathering resistance and flexibility in cold climates

runs.v: PVC Roofing Systems

PVC is a durable membrane that resists chemicals, grease, and punctures, setting it apart from other single ply options in environments where rooftop exhaust carries oils or solvents. Like TPO, PVC features heat-welded seams and a white reflective surface that helps reduce energy consumption and meet local energy codes. PVC consistently earns Class A fire ratings, which is critical for schools, healthcare facilities, and buildings near industrial zones.
In NJ,

run approximately $7 to $14 per square foot, with a 20,000-square-foot project-such as a restaurant complex or processing facility-costing $120,000 to $200,000 fully installed. Expected lifespan is 25 to 35 years. The main long-term concern is plasticizer loss, which can cause edge embrittlement after many years of service, though modern formulations have improved plasticizer stability significantly.

runs.v: Built-Up Roofing (BUR) and Modified Bitumen Systems

Built-Up Roofing (BUR) consists of multiple layers of bitumen and reinforcing felt, creating a redundant waterproofing system that has protected commercial buildings for over a century. Modified Bitumen is an asphalt-based, multi-ply system that resists tears, using polymer-modified sheets with reinforcement for improved flexibility. Both remain common on older Newark schools, municipal buildings, and mid-century warehouses where their toughness under foot traffic and heavy equipment is valued.

Built-up roofing systems cost between $5 and $9 per square foot for materials, with fully installed commercial systems in Newark ranging from $7 to $12+ per square foot. Built-up roofing systems offer excellent water intrusion protection through their layered redundancy. Service life is typically 20 to 30 years for well-maintained BUR;
somewhat less at 15 to 25 years depending on exposure and maintenance. These systems are heavier than single-ply, requiring verification of deck load capacity.

runs.v: Metal Roofing for Commercial Properties

Metal roofing can last 40 to 70 years with minimal maintenance, making it the longest-lived option in the commercial roofing industry. Standing seam systems, architectural metal panels, and metal retrofit panels serve retail facades, churches, transit facilities, and mixed-use buildings throughout Newark. A
excels at snow shedding, resists fire, and offers significant aesthetic value for visible building surfaces.

Metal roofing costs range from $7 to $12 per square foot for materials, with fully installed standing seam systems in NJ commonly reaching $12 to $18+ per square foot when structural reinforcement, detailed flashings, and corrosion protection are factored in. In Newark, where older buildings may need deck reinforcement and attention to thermal expansion joints, the installation process requires experienced roofing contractors with metal-specific expertise. Despite the steep initial cost, the long term performance and minimal maintenance requirements make metal roofing among the most cost effective solutions over a 50-year horizon.

items.v: Best for steep-slope entry canopies, visible corporate facades, and transit facilities
Excellent resistance to rust when properly coated or specified in aluminum
Strong snow shedding performance for Newark's winter conditions
Properties aiming for modern aesthetics with decades of durability

runs.v: Spray Polyurethane Foam (SPF) and Elastomeric Roof Coatings

SPF is a sprayed insulation and waterproofing system that creates a seamless surface over existing roofs, while elastomeric coatings-acrylic, silicone, and urethane formulations-serve as restoration options to extend the life of aging membranes. Roof coatings can restore aging roofs without a complete tear-off, making them attractive for building owners who need to spread capital costs or whose existing membrane is still structurally sound.

in NJ cost roughly $4 to $8 per square foot for the foam layer, with total system costs higher when protective topcoats are included. Coating-only restorations run approximately $3.50 to $7.00 per square foot installed and can add 10 to 15 years of service life when the substrate is properly prepared. SPF can exceed 30 years of service life if topcoat maintenance is performed on schedule. The key risk with coatings and SPF is that underlying deck or insulation problems may be hidden-thorough moisture scanning before application is essential.

Cost effective life extension for roofs where the field membrane is still sound

runs.v: Green, Cool, and Solar-Ready Roofing Solutions

Cool roofing systems lower building temperatures and energy consumption by reflecting solar radiation rather than absorbing it. White TPO and PVC membranes inherently qualify as cool roofs, but dedicated cool-roof coatings and reflective cap sheets can also be applied to existing systems. In a dense urban environment like Newark, where the heat island effect raises summer rooftop temperatures, reflectivity pays off quickly. Green roofs improve air quality and reduce urban heat, adding vegetation over a waterproof membrane assembly-though structural capacity must support the added weight (green roofing systems can cost between $10 and $25 per square foot).

Solar-ready assemblies are increasingly common on new construction and major retrofits. These are designed from the outset to support PV arrays with proper ballast distribution, reinforced penetration flashing, and

that remain valid even after solar installation. Newark Quality Roofing coordinates with solar installers to ensure membrane integrity and warranty coverage remain intact. Green roofing systems improve air quality and insulation while contributing to sustainability goals.

Leaks Around Rooftop Equipment and Penetrations

HVAC curbs, vent stacks, skylights, satellite mounts, and any other roof penetration are the most frequent leak sources on commercial flat roofs. Flashings around these elements degrade faster than field membrane because of thermal movement, vibration, and damage from mechanical contractors who access the roof for equipment servicing.

after any mechanical contractor works on the roof. Newark Quality Roofing recommends protective walk pads along common access routes to protect membrane integrity.
Ponding Water and Drainage Failures

Older Newark commercial buildings frequently have flat roofs with insufficient slope, clogged internal drains, or sagging deck areas that retain standing water. Flat or low-slope roofs require membrane systems that effectively shed water, and ponding accelerates membrane aging, adds structural load, and is a leading cause of leaks.

: Reworking drains and scuppers during re-roofing, installing tapered insulation to create proper slope, using SPF overlays to build drainage paths, and implementing regular drain cleaning schedules. Even minor repairs to drainage components can prevent major water damage. Newark Quality Roofing addresses drainage as a priority on every
and restoration project.
Membrane Blisters, Punctures, and Foot Traffic Damage

Blisters form in BUR and modified bitumen roofs when moisture becomes trapped between plies. Punctures result from dropped tools, loose gravel, and repeated foot traffic by maintenance staff accessing rooftop equipment. Heavy rooftop traffic may require durable roofing materials that resist punctures-and even the most durable membranes benefit from protective measures.

: Install reinforced walk pads along paths to HVAC units, apply localized patches and reinforcement at damaged areas, and establish roof access protocols that train building staff and outside contractors on safe practices.

Age-Related Failure and Code-Driven Replacement

Many commercial roofs in Newark built before the early 2000s are at or beyond their typical service life. New NJ energy codes often require higher insulation R-values during any roof replacement, meaning that simply replacing the membrane is rarely sufficient-the entire assembly must be brought up to current standards. Emergency roofing services are essential for commercial properties where sudden failures threaten operations. Emergency repairs can prevent further damage to properties while a permanent solution is designed.

: Full tear-off and installation of a code-compliant new system is the most reliable path when insulation and decking show moisture damage. When underlying layers are still sound, restoration with coatings or SPF can extend service life at lower cost. Newark Quality Roofing helps clients phase projects and budget over multiple fiscal years, ensuring each phase delivers measurable protection and compliance.

There is no one-size-fits-all answer in commercial roofing. The right solution blends building type, current roof condition, budget, energy goals, and long-term maintenance planning. A TPO or PVC membrane might deliver the best balance of energy savings and durability for a retail plaza, while a restored BUR system makes more financial sense for a warehouse with a sound existing assembly. What remains constant across every project is the need for thorough inspection, expert system design, and quality installation followed by consistent maintenance.
